mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute Team A's historical shots-FOR to shots_on_target-FOR ratio (all-prior) and Team B's shots-AGAINST to shots_on_target-AGAINST ratio (all-prior and recent-5). Condition on the joint cross-team pairing of these two ratios simultaneously — neither ratio alone, but their product/interaction — to assess whether the combined on-target volume rises or is suppressed relative to competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total match shots-on-target rises when both Team A's own conversion ratio and Team B's allowed conversion ratio are jointly elevated; suppressed when either ratio is jointly low — the joint product diverges from what either single-observable mirror would predict independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) jointly with Team B's defensive shot-suppression ratio (shots AGAINST vs shots_on_target AGAINST) determines the combined on-target shot volume in the match. When one side produces many shots but a low fraction on target while the opponent allows many shots but a high fraction on target, the joint interaction — not either observable alone — shapes total shots-on-target.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for two different sides in an asymmetric cross-team pairing. It is not reducible to a single observable compared against what an opponent allows, nor to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks FOR into first-half and second-half averages for Team A; split corner_kicks AGAINST into first-half and second-half averages for Team B. Condition on the joint half-level pairing: whether both teams show a second-half-skewed corner profile simultaneously, versus a first-half-skewed or balanced profile.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half corner volume rises above the full-match per-half average when Team A's second-half corner production rate exceeds its first-half rate AND Team B's second-half corner concession rate exceeds its first-half rate jointly; the relationship is suppressed when the half-level profiles are misaligned.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team A's first-half corner production and second-half corner production (a within-match half-level split) interacts with Team B's corresponding half-level corner concession pattern to determine whether corner volume is front-loaded or back-loaded in this specific fixture. When Team A generates more corners in the second half than the first, and Team B concedes more corners in the second half than the first, the second-half corner total is jointly amplified beyond what full-match averages suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This uses within-match half-level resolution (first-half vs second-half splits) for two distinct observables (Team A FOR and Team B AGAINST) simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one coarse band, nor a simple home/away or recent/long-run split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's historical yellow_cards FOR rate and Team A's historical fouls AGAINST rate (fouls drawn). The mechanism activates when both are simultaneously elevated relative to competition baseline — a two-observable, two-team asymmetric joint condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B yellow cards rise when Team B's own yellow card rate and Team A's foul-drawing rate are jointly above competition baseline; the relationship is weaker when only one of the two conditions holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's yellow card accumulation rate (yellow_cards FOR) jointly with Team A's foul-drawing rate (fouls AGAINST — fouls committed against Team A, i.e. fouls drawn by Team A) determines the disciplinary pressure on Team B in this fixture. When Team B commits fouls at an elevated rate AND Team A draws fouls at an elevated rate, the joint interaction predicts elevated yellow card volume for Team B beyond what either observable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-observable relationship: Team B's yellow cards are conditioned jointly on Team B's own foul tendency AND Team A's foul-drawing tendency — two distinct observables across two different teams. Not reducible to one observable mirrored against what an opponent allows.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) the possession imbalance between Team A (home) and Team B (away) using both all-prior and recent-5 windows, and (b) the drift in Team A's corner production (recent-5 vs all-prior) alongside Team B's corner concession drift (recent-5 vs all-prior). The mechanism tests whether possession advantage reliably converts to corner advantage, or whether recent drift in corner rates decouples the two.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner volume for Team A rises with possession advantage when Team A's recent corner production rate has not declined relative to its long-run rate; when recent corner production has drifted downward despite stable possession, the possession-to-corner relationship saturates or decouples.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between possession differential (Team A possession FOR minus Team B possession FOR, i.e. the possession imbalance) and corner kick differential determines whether possession dominance translates into corner dominance. When Team A holds more possession at home but its corner production has recently declined (recent-5 vs all-prior), while Team B concedes more corners recently, the possession-to-corner translation efficiency is the joint mechanism of interest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) incorporating a regime/drift dimension (recent-5 vs all-prior window comparison) for both teams simultaneously. Not reducible to either observable alone with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split goals FOR into first-half and second-half averages for Team A; split goals AGAINST into first-half and second-half averages for Team B. Condition on the joint half-level pairing: whether Team A's second-half scoring rate exceeds its first-half rate AND Team B's second-half concession rate exceeds its first-half rate simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal volume rises above the per-half average when Team A's second-half scoring rate is higher than its first-half rate AND Team B's second-half concession rate is higher than its first-half rate jointly; the effect is attenuated when the half-level profiles are misaligned between the two teams.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's goals-FOR half-level split (first-half vs second-half scoring rate) and Team B's goals-AGAINST half-level split (first-half vs second-half concession rate) determines whether goal-scoring is concentrated in a particular half. When Team A scores more in the second half than the first, and Team B concedes more in the second half than the first, the second-half goal volume is jointly amplified — an asymmetric cross-team, within-match state mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This uses within-match half-level resolution (first-half vs second-half splits) applied asymmetrically across two teams (Team A FOR and Team B AGAINST) simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one coarse band, nor a simple venue or recent/long-run split.
